{
  "schemaVersion": "authorization-migration-public-policy/v1",
  "repository": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea",
  "sourceRef": "fc28937a8d772fe9e4025c9b5f24d5db4d86610b",
  "upstreamSources": [
    "routers/api/v1/api.go#L451-L459,L1741-L1745",
    "routers/api/v1/repo/issue_lock.go#L15-L81"
  ],
  "normativePolicy": "The issue-lock route requires the caller to be a repository administrator or site administrator. After that route gate, the handler also requires permission to write the issue or pull request before it may lock an unlocked issue.",
  "boundedScenario": "The caller is authenticated, has full token scope and repository issue-write permission, but is neither a repository administrator nor a site administrator; the issue exists, is readable, and is currently unlocked.",
  "claimBoundary": "The assessment concerns the declared API route and fixed source only. It does not infer deployment state or permissions outside the supplied scenario."
}

results.explanation: The declared policy expectation is enforced on the supplied path, so the expected deny-nonadmin failure is refuted. The PUT lock entry is grouped under reqToken and reqAdmin; reqAdmin checks repository- or site-administrator status and returns forbidden when both are false. Under the fixed scenario, the principal is authenticated but is neither kind of administrator, so this upstream gate stops the request before LockIssue. The handler separately checks issue or pull-request write permission against the retrieved issue, but that later gate cannot bypass the earlier administrator gate. The lock effect is reachable only after the permission check and, because the target is declared unlocked, through the unlocked branch; the locked-state branch that skips the effect is not applicable. For the object comparison, reqAdmin checks the requester's repository/site-admin relationship, not ownership of or permission on the issue; CanWriteIssuesOrPulls is evaluated in the handler for the retrieved issue and is the source-visible issue-related gate. No owner, collaborator-admin, or site-admin exception applies under the stated principal facts; those exceptions are the conditions described by reqAdmin, not permission inherited from issue-write access. No source-external fact is decisive for this bounded result: changing the administrator-status observation would change the outcome—if repository or site administrator, the first gate would pass and the issue-write check would then matter; if neither, the request is denied before the lock effect. The minimum observation is the requester's repository- and site-administrator status, already supplied by the scenario.

condition.statement: The lock operation is entered only when the retrieved issue is not already locked; the supplied target is declared unlocked.

No decisive source-external fact is needed to change this bounded result: under the supplied nonadmin conditions, the route guard blocks the effect. entry.statement: The declared lock operation is bound to the PUT route in the shown lock route group, and the route applies token and administrator middleware before dispatching to the lock handler.

binding.statement: The route requires a token, the administrator control evaluates the request context, and the handler supplies the context user as the doer of the lock operation; the fixed source does not show a separate identity-resolution implementation.

The requested issue is selected by the repository ID in the request context together with the integer index path parameter; the selected issue is then the issue checked and passed to the lock options. The repository object assigned before mutation is a distinct checked repository context object, not an ownership-based substitute for the issue permission check.

control.statement: The strongest visible authorization control is reqAdmin: it permits route progress only when either repository-administrator or site-administrator status is true; otherwise it returns forbidden.

After route admission, the handler separately requires issue-write permission for the selected issue or pull; the declared issue-writer condition satisfies this weaker gate but not the administrator gate.

effect.statement: The visible nonadministrator branch returns a forbidden API response before handler dispatch, while the successful handler path returns no content after the optional lock mutation.

If all upstream controls permitted progress, the handler would call the lock operation only when the selected issue is not already locked; that protected mutation is therefore unreachable for the declared nonadministrator caller.

These conditions make the route-level administrator denial applicable and make the no-op locked branch inapplicable only hypothetically; the request does not reach either handler branch after route denial.

The runtime authorization identity is checked for repository-administrator or site-administrator status, and the declared principal has neither status.
The handler selects the issue using the repository context and the request path issue index, binding the selected object to the declared existing issue scenario.
The repository context used to resolve the issue is distinct from the issue object selected by its path index and is also used when assigning the issue repository before mutation.

citations.quote:
reason := web.GetForm[*api.LockIssueOption](ctx).Reason
	issue, err := issues_model.GetIssueByIndex(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository.ID, ctx.PathParamInt64("index"))

issue.Repo = ctx.Repo.Repository
		err = issues_model.LockIssue(ctx, opt)

control.statement: After the route guard, the handler separately requires issue-write permission for the selected issue and returns forbidden when absent.

The strongest visible authorization control is the pre-handler requirement that the caller pass either repository-administrator or site-administrator status; otherwise the route returns forbidden and stops.

effect.statement: Only after the issue-write check, and only when the issue is not locked, does the handler construct lock options and invoke the lock mutation; the unlocked condition makes this the relevant permitted branch, but the failed route guard prevents reaching it for the declared principal.

If both route authorization and issue-write checks pass, the handler reports no content after the optional lock mutation; this branch is unavailable to the declared nonadministrator because the route guard stops first.

condition.statement: The bounded scenario supplies authentication, issue existence/readability, issue-write permission, unlocked state, and absence of both administrator roles; the source-visible administrator guard therefore fails before the handler path.

scopeClaim.statement: Only declared obligations and supplied fixed source are assessed; discovery is not tested.

task.request: Determine whether an authenticated repository issue writer with full token scope, but with neither repository-administrator nor site-administrator status, may lock an existing unlocked issue through PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/lock.

policySources.text: The issue-lock route requires repository-administrator or site-administrator status; the handler then also requires issue-write permission before locking an unlocked issue.

acceptance.reason: The fixed public route and handler expose both permission gates before the lock mutation.

principals.role: authenticated repository issue writer without an administrator role
principals.description: Author facts: ["The caller has full token scope and repository issue-write permission, but is neither a repository administrator nor a site administrator."]

resources.description: Author facts: ["An existing readable issue whose lock state is currently unlocked."]
